name: Round John Lennon glasses

card.summary: Thin round wire-frame glasses that soften angular faces and add a vintage, intellectual look.

quick.overview:
Round John Lennon glasses are thin, perfectly circular metal frames, named for the musician who made the style famous. They are worn as a style accessory or as corrective eyewear.

People choose them to add a rounded shape against an angular jaw or boxy face, and for a retro, artistic impression. Beyond fashion writing, little formal research exists on how frame shape changes perceived attractiveness.
quick.how: Worn as ordinary prescription or non-prescription glasses, usually in a metal frame with thin rims, in gold, silver or black.
quick.risks: No health risks beyond ordinary eyewear; frames that do not fit can slip or press on the nose and temples.

lead: Round John Lennon glasses are perfectly round metal-framed spectacles, a style named after musician John Lennon and also nicknamed "Harry Potter" glasses.[1] Wearers use them for a vintage, bookish or artistic look.

Wikipedia notes that rounded frames, with perfectly round ones the most efficient, suit strongly nearsighted prescriptions, and that glasses overall moved from stigma to fashion item in the twentieth century.[1] Style guides commonly suggest round frames as a contrast to angular face shapes; no controlled studies are known.

chain: Thin round frame adds curved lines
angle.text: Wearers put on the frames to change the visual shape of the face and to add a retro, creative style. The effect lasts while the glasses are worn.

paras: The style is a thin-rimmed, circular metal frame, often with a keyhole or saddle bridge.[1]
The shape is associated with John Lennon, as thick horn-rimmed frames are with Buddy Holly.[1] Glasses in general were long seen as unfashionable before the stigma eased in the early 1900s.[1]
